contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, DAG and principles
Shared needs: what the shared author declares for this node
Mechanism: tickets as store entities, deps and file claims evaluated every tick
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries up to 3, then recover and report
State paths and the cleanup script for each

N-06 Service unit, clock and health
pointers.principle: Rule 1 (input to output: a ticket declares what starts and ends it) and rule 4 (tickets live in the store, never the repository)
The collision answer every node gives: leases with fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, idempotent steps, 409 that reports
pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for ticket.admitted 100; ticket.waiting 100; intake.recovered 100; ticket.ready 200; ticket.done 204; ticket.cancelled 204; ticket.transition_refused 409; ticket.refused 422; ticket.stale 500; intake.failed 500; intake.orphan 500; intake.slow 500. Owner-acts: ticket.stale; intake.orphan at three in a day.

tickets(id PRIMARY KEY, status, phase, attempt, priority, role, files JSON, deps JSON, body JSON, cut_at, ready_at, done_at, version); the closed status set cut, waiting, ready, in_flight, done, dead, cancelled, refused and its transition table.
claims(path PRIMARY KEY, ticket, taken_at, released_at); taken in the ticket.ready transaction, released in the terminal transaction.
Entity flag:hold set by N-29; read at the start of every tick by N-03, N-07 and N-09; ticks and monitoring never stop under hold.
One file, one in-flight ticket: files declared at cut, refused at ready, claim rows as the proof (V07, memory rule one-file-one-in-flight-ticket).
One concern, a few files, a diff read in minutes; when in doubt split (V09, owner 2026-10-13 03:00Z).
The ticket as data: id, title (never a bare id), files, deps, role, acceptance commands with exit codes, input, output, priority; the seat reads it with ticket get and never changes it.
intake.stale_days 7, intake.evaluate_seconds 2, intake.keep_days 90; the aggregate exemption list factory/config/claims.json carried as data.
A ticket waiting past intake.stale_days: ticket.stale 500 on the daily tick, one card; the owner cancels or re-cuts through N-29.

purpose.is: N-03 holds every ticket as an entity in the store (D04 option C, C35: tickets in the state root, never in git) and decides, on every tick, which tickets are ready: every dependency done, and no declared file claimed by another ticket in flight.
It takes the file claim atomically when it says ready, so two tickets can never be ready on one file (V07: one file, one in-flight ticket, declared at cut and refused at start).
purpose.is-not: It does not cut tickets (an AI does, as data: N-17), does not validate acceptance commands (N-18), does not dispatch (N-07) and never reads a ticket from a branch or the main checkout (RC3, K07).
purpose.decisions: D04 (C35), D16 (C48: AI cuts, validator approves before a cut is allowed), V07, V09 (small tickets), the one-file-one-in-flight-ticket memory rule.

record.who: N-18 validator (accepted ticket records from a ticket-set.draft; every new ticket enters here and only here); N-29 (a ruling that unblocks a dead ticket, re-entered with attempt reset). A ticket.request is not a ticket and enters by the record below.
record.field: WO-YYYYMMDD-xxxx, minted by the store's id verb, unique by UNIQUE index.
Full title; a bare id is a defect (global rule: never name a ticket without its title).
Declared paths or globs the ticket may change; empty is refused (claims.sh choice 1, kept).
Ticket ids that must be done first; a cycle is refused (work-order dependency graph with cycle refusal, L11 section 8).
The role of the worker phase.
Commands with expected exit codes, as N-18 ran them on main; stored, not re-run here.
What starts and what ends the ticket, as the DAG rule requires of every node (dag.md section 7 rule 1).
Integer; lower first; the owner's rulings may set it.

record.who: N-10 (a fix for a held main: reason fix-for-hold, rejected_id, hold_id), N-30 (rule R05: a cut: or ticket: message, the text as the brief), N-49 (one per LAND row: title, files, acceptance from the row), N-50 (the archive ticket of the fourteen cancels).
record.field: The request id (the idempotency key: one per message id, LAND row, hold id plus fix attempt, or cancel set), the record that caused it, the design anchor or row it is about, a full title, the brief text.
Hints the spec-author may use; none is trusted: the ticket the request becomes is cut by N-17 and validated by N-18 on main (D16).
record.rule: Admit turns a request into a cut-request entity CR-<request id> with status ready, phase spec, role spec-author, attempt 1, no files and no claims (a spec-author's workspace is read-only, N-14), and appends ticket.ready 200 for it; N-02 leases CR-<id>:spec:n and N-07 dispatches the spec-author (N-17). The entity is done when N-18 writes ticket-set.accepted naming it as source_request, and dead after three validator.refused (N-11). A second request with the same id replays (200); a fix request naming a hold that already has a live cut request is refused 409 (nodes/N-10/spec.xml#many-agents).

also.note: every tick re-evaluates every waiting ticket (level-triggered)

also.from: N-09 merge, N-11 dead, N-29 or N-50 cancel
also.note: terminal states that free deps and claims

record.field: What N-02 claims. Phase is worker for a new ticket and spec for a cut request (CR key, role spec-author); the reviewer phase re-enters on gate.verdict green (N-08) and the merge phase on review.passed (N-19).
The paths claimed in the same transaction.
Pointers the seat bundle (N-13) renders: the ticket entity key and the design anchor.
deps (with the ids not yet done), files (with the paths and the holder), hold (flag:hold set), gate (a pull request awaits its coq/gate verdict), validation (schema failure at intake, with the path).
record.rule: ticket.waiting is written once per transition of reason, not every tick: the entity carries the reason and the record is appended only when it changes, so the log stays readable and N-31 pushes a change, not a heartbeat.

output.record: Cycle in deps, unknown dep id, empty files, or a file that is an aggregate the repository never claims; the ticket entity is written with status refused so the cut is visible and one card is not raised (N-17 retries with the refusal attached, up to 3).

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/intake: Admit, Evaluate, Claim, Release, Terminal. Pure functions: cycle check (Kahn), overlap check (the claims.sh pattern rule), readiness predicate. Writes through N-01 Put with entity writes.

tickets (id PRIMARY KEY, status, phase, attempt, priority, role, files JSON, deps JSON, body JSON, cut_at, ready_at, done_at, version); claims (path PRIMARY KEY, ticket, taken_at, released_at); both in coq.db, owned here.
cut, waiting, ready, in_flight (a lease is live), done, dead, cancelled, refused. Closed set (L11 section 8: closed status set kept); a transition not in the table is 409.
mechanism.mermaid: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> cut: Admit (schema ok, no cycle) cut --> refused: cycle, empty files, unknown dep (422) cut --> waiting: deps or files not free (100) waiting --> ready: deps done and files free, claims taken (200) cut --> ready: all free at admit ready --> in_flight: lease.granted (N-02) in_flight --> waiting: lease.expired or seat.result blocked, attempt lt 3 (N-11) in_flight --> ready: phase change (N-08 green, N-19 passed) in_flight --> done: merge record (N-09) in_flight --> dead: attempt 3 failed (N-11) dead --> waiting: ruling unblocks (N-29), attempt reset waiting --> cancelled: ruling or cut-over (N-29, N-50) done --> [*] cancelled --> [*]
mechanism.step: Admit (a ticket; a ticket.request is admitted by its own rule under #input, as a cut request with no files): validate against record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket; refuse empty files; refuse any file matching the aggregate list (factory/config/claims.json, kept as data); check every dep id exists; run the cycle check over deps plus the existing graph; write the entity with status cut or refused; append ticket.admitted 100 or ticket.refused 422.

Evaluate (every scheduler tick, and at once after Admit): for every ticket with status cut or waiting, in priority then cut_at order: deps_done is true when every dep has status done; files_free is true when no claim row with released_at null matches any declared path by the overlap rule; hold is flag:hold.

Ready: when deps_done and files_free and not hold, in one Put transaction: INSERT a claim row per declared path with expected_version 0 (a race on any path makes the whole transaction 409 and the ticket stays waiting this tick), set status ready, ready_at, append ticket.ready 200.
Waiting: when not ready, compute the reason; if it differs from the entity's stored reason, write the entity and append ticket.waiting 100; else write nothing.

Terminal: on merge record (N-09) set done and release every claim of the ticket (released_at) in the same transaction; on dead (N-11) release claims and set dead; on cancel set cancelled and release. Released claims are what N-45 reads to free branches and worktrees.

Phase: lease.released on a worker phase with a pr.opened record sets the ticket waiting with reason gate (no claim is offered while the pods run); gate.verdict green 201 on the ticket's current head (N-08) moves phase to reviewer and the ticket to ready for the reviewer claim, so no reviewer is ever leased on an ungated head; gate.verdict red 422 goes to N-11 and the worker's next attempt; review.passed 201 on the same head moves phase to merge, which no seat claims (N-09 merges on the records). One phase change per phase per ticket; a second is 409 ticket.transition_refused.
mechanism.overlap: Two patterns overlap when either matches the other's literal prefix; `*` crosses `/`; a bare directory or a trailing `/` means the subtree (factory/bin/claims.sh header, kept verbatim as the rule).
mechanism.ordering: Priority first, then cut_at; within one tick the evaluation is a single pass, so a lower-priority ticket cannot take a file a higher one needs in the same tick.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. Admit runs when a ticket record commits (N-01 Tail in-process); Evaluate runs on every scheduler tick from N-06 and once after each Admit and each Terminal; nothing waits for a prompt.
start.step: At service start, after the store opens: Recover reads every claim row with released_at null whose ticket is done, dead or cancelled and releases it, appending intake.recovered 100 with the count. This is the automation of "clear a routed-ledger entry by hand" (L02 section 7 item 1).
Tickets in status ready with no live lease stay ready; N-07's first tick dispatches them.

wait.name: deps
wait.timeout: none held here: the ticket waits as data; ticket.waiting carries the ids
wait.fallback: N-51's daily tick reports a ticket waiting over intake.stale_days 7 as ticket.stale 500 to N-28; the owner decides cancel or re-cut

wait.name: files
wait.fallback: same as deps: stale report after intake.stale_days; the holder's own lease and stall timers bound how long a claim can be held in flight

wait.name: hold
wait.fallback: the owner clears it through N-42 and N-29; the Controls screen shows the lamp

wait.name: put
wait.fallback: 503; retried per retries; the ticket is evaluated again next tick

wait.name: evaluate
wait.fallback: a pass over the bound is cut at the bound, intake.slow 500 is reported once, and the rest are evaluated next tick in order

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: A store 503 is retried 3 times with 1, 2, 4 s; the fourth failure appends intake.failed 500 and the ticket record is re-admitted on the next Tail re-read, because Admit is idempotent by the ticket id.
A 409 on a claim row (another ticket took the path this tick) is not an error: the ticket stays waiting with reason files; no retry inside the tick; next tick re-evaluates.
A refused ticket goes back to its author as data: N-17 retries with the refusal attached up to 3 times (dag.md section 4, N-18 bound), then N-11 writes dead and N-28 raises one card.
A merge record whose ticket cannot be found appends intake.orphan 500 with the PR number and does not fail the merge; N-28 raises a card only if three orphans occur in a day.

many-agents.reading: Twenty seats read their own ticket entity by key through the ctl CLI; the ticket body is one JSON entity, versioned; a seat never reads work-orders/ from a branch.
many-agents.working: Many authors (N-17 runs) admit tickets at once: each Admit is one transaction keyed by ticket id; two drafts naming the same id collide on the UNIQUE index and the second is 409, so a ticket set is admitted exactly once.
many-agents.collision: Two waiting tickets declare overlapping paths and both become eligible in one tick: the single pass evaluates in priority order and the first takes the claim rows; the second's claim transaction is 409 on the shared path and it stays waiting with reason files naming the holder.

A merge releases claims while Evaluate runs: both are transactions behind the single writer; Evaluate either sees the released row and claims, or sees the live row and waits one tick. Never both tickets in flight on the path.

N-29 unblocks a dead ticket while N-11 is writing dead for attempt 3: the entity version guards the transition; the loser gets 409 and re-reads; the table of allowed transitions means dead then waiting (ruling) is legal and waiting then dead is not, so the ruling wins by the second write.
N-17 round 1 and its retry both submit the same ticket: the id is the same, Admit is idempotent, one entity exists.
many-agents.test: 100 tickets over 20 shared paths with random deps and no cycle, admitted by 4 concurrent writers, evaluated over 50 ticks with merges released at random: at no tick are two in-flight tickets holding one path; every ticket reaches ready exactly once per phase.

emits.note: reason deps, files, hold, validation; once per reason change
emits.acts: nobody; N-38 shows the queue depth
N-45 (branch and worktree release), N-51 (the day's verified count)
monitoring; a card at three in a day

status-codes.rule: ticket.dead is written by N-11, not here. Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-tickets.sh: --dry-run lists done, cancelled and refused tickets older than intake.keep_days 90 and their released claims; --apply deletes them after N-05 confirms a verified backup newer than their done_at

path.writer: `scheduler ctl ticket export` only, a read-only rendering for humans; never read by any node

state-paths.rule: work-orders/ in the repository stops being a ticket store at GOFACTORY (N-50): existing files are rendered into the store once by N-49's land dispositions, and the directory holds no status thereafter.

a fix ticket after rejected main

a message turned into a ticket request
land tickets, one per LAND row

actor.may: Admit tickets of their re-entry kinds; N-29 may set priority and unblock

actor.name: seat (the model)
actor.may: `scheduler ctl ticket get` of its own ticket; nothing else; it cannot change status, files or deps (that is a draft to N-17 and N-18)

actor.may: cancel, reprioritize and unblock through cards (N-29); `scheduler ctl ticket export` for reading

counter.name: tickets.refused_total

monitoring.surface: Map screen (N-38) shows queue depth per status as belt load; Machine screen (N-39) shows one ticket's deps and claims; Alerts (N-41) shows ticket.stale.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl ticket get WO-ID` prints status, reason, the dep ids not done and the paths with their holders.
`scheduler ctl ticket export --dir STATE/tickets/export` writes one markdown per ticket; the directory is disposable.
Through a card and N-29, never by editing the store; the ruling record is the audit.

item.what: tickets in work-orders/ in git with a status field, cut as PRs (option A), or status in a store with body in git (B), or GitHub issues (D)
item.reason: C35 ruled option C; every RC3 symptom came from status on a branch; issues would be read over the network every tick

item.what: finding live tickets through `git worktree list` and open PRs with gh
item.reason: the claim is a row here, taken at ready and released at merge; the overlap rule and the aggregate exemption are kept as data; `claims.sh diff` survives as the gate's stray-path check in N-25's volume

item.what: a directory queue with claim by atomic rename
item.reason: one queue with lanes was the rule (L02 section 7 item 9); the tickets table with priority order is that queue; claim-by-rename's safety for two pullers is replaced by the store's compare-and-swap

item.what: the second directory queue, read by the board
item.reason: same reason: three queues meant three truths (K05); the board reads the tickets table through N-31

item.what: the third directory queue, the architect's
item.reason: same reason; an architect never holds a queue (owner 2026-10-13: the architect keeps the line running without doing the work); rulings are records through N-29

item.what: work-order skill scripts bound to a single checkout
item.reason: re-homed: closed status set, dependency graph with cycle refusal and evidence gates are kept as the tickets table and Admit; the bash and the single-checkout assumption are not

item.what: start flips status on the ticket's branch
item.reason: status never lives in git again (K07); ready is a store transition

item.what: an agent decides a ticket is done after its PR merged and cuts a close PR
item.reason: item 6: the merge record sets the terminal state in the same transaction
